items.title: Does the adult divisional clinical examination still reflect how physicians practise? A qualitative study of Royal Australasian College of Physicians Fellows' and trainees' perceptions.
items.abstract: The Royal Australasian College of Physicians' (RACP) clinical examination remains a high-stakes barrier assessment for physician trainees in Australia and Aotearoa New Zealand. Its bedside long case and short case tasks are largely unchanged, despite a renewed basic training curriculum and advancing clinical practice, raising the question of whether the clinical examination still reflects how physicians practise. To explore fellows' and trainees' perceptions of how well the clinical examination's bedside tasks align to contemporary physician practice. Purposive then snowball sampling recruited 10 fellows and five trainees across Australia and Aotearoa New Zealand. Semi-structured interviews, conducted until information power was reached, were analysed using reflexive thematic analysis. The long case was consistently valued as an authentic test of physician practice. Short case alignment was specialty-dependent: neurology was perceived as having enduring validity, whereas cardiology least reflected modern practice. Participants described real-world practice as hypothesis-driven rather than a formulaic, system-based routine and valued the clinical examination not only as an assessment of competence but as a shared experience that shapes professional identity. To our knowledge, this is the first study to assess the clinical examination through Kane's extrapolation inference. This work suggests a shift towards hypothesis-driven short case examination, prioritising manoeuvres because they reflect contemporary clinical management; it could enhance the clinical examination's validity while retaining the long case as the most valid component. Reform must also recognise the clinical examination's dual role in assessing competence and forming professional identity.

items.title: Short- and Mid-Term Effects of Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement on Heart Rate Variability in Patients With Aortic Valve Stenosis.
items.abstract: Heart rate variability (HRV) reflects autonomic nervous system balance and has emerged as a potential prognostic marker in cardiovascular diseases. However, the relationship between HRV and mortality following transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) remains unclear. This prospective cohort study included 230 patients with symptomatic severe aortic stenosis who underwent TAVR between June 2022 and June 2024. Twenty-four-hour Holter electrocardiography recordings were obtained one day before and at 3 months after the procedure to assess HRV using both time- and frequency-domain parameters. Among the 230 patients enrolled, the 12-month all-cause mortality rate was 14.3%. Among frequency-domain parameters, the pre-TAVR low frequency/high frequency (LF/HF) ratio improved markedly from 2.20±1.45 to 1.54±0.85 (p 2 , 0.285). Patients with a pre-TAVR LF/HF ratio>1.34 had significantly lower mortality at follow-up (hazard ratio [HR] 0.103; 95% CI 0.042-0.250; log-rank p<0.001), and this association remained significant in landmark analysis beyond 3 months (HR 0.163; log-rank p<0.001). HRV parameters provide meaningful prognostic information in patients undergoing TAVR. Among them, a reduced pre-TAVR LF/HF ratio is independently associated with increased 1-year mortality and may serve as a practical, non-invasive marker for risk stratification.

items.title: Predicting Gastrointestinal Complications After Cardiac Surgery From Mean Arterial Blood Pressure Under a Data-Driven Threshold for Hypotension: Protocol for an Advanced Database Study.
items.abstract: Hypotension during cardiopulmonary bypass may increase the risk of gastrointestinal complications due to insufficient splanchnic autoregulatory capacity. We hypothesize that both duration and level of blood pressure below a data-driven threshold during cardiopulmonary bypass are associated with the risk of gastrointestinal complications. Patients who underwent cardiac surgery at Copenhagen University Hospital, Rigshospitalet, during 2018-2022 will be included if they underwent on-pump valve surgery, coronary artery bypass grafting, and/or surgery on the ascending aorta. The primary outcome is major gastrointestinal complications within 30 days, defined as acute intestinal ischemia, abdominal surgery, bowel perforation, or gastrointestinal hemorrhage. Secondary endpoints are serious gastrointestinal complications, delayed recovery of bowel function, cholinesterase inhibitor administration, and 30-day mortality. The exposure is the exposure to lower blood pressure, calculated as the product of the duration and level of blood pressure below a data-driven threshold. To identify the optimal threshold, we split the population in a training (75%) and validation cohort (25%). In the training cohort we will identify the threshold with the highest area under the receiver operating curve for the primary outcome. The selected threshold will then be applied to quantify the exposure to lower blood pressure for each patient. Patients will be grouped using a modified Youden's index (weighing sensitivity 80%) as a cutoff for high versus low exposure to lower blood pressure, and association with the study endpoints will be determined in the validation cohort. Under the assumption of pressure-dependent perfusion outside of an autoregulatory plateau, the exposure to blood pressure below a threshold might reflect the risk of gastrointestinal complications more accurately than point measures or averages. The results from this study may lead to relevant hypotheses for prospective testing.

items.title: Automated Detection of Abnormal Pediatric Electroencephalograms Using Machine Learning: Retrospective Study.
items.abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) is widely used in medicine as a technique for the assessment of several brain-related pathologies. However, EEG interpretation requires specialized expertise and remains a labor-intensive task, particularly for prolonged recordings in intensive care, where timely expert review is often challenging. The aim of this study is to address this problem by using AI methods to automate EEG interpretation and compare the performance of different modeling approaches. A gradient boosting-based model, inspired by the work of Albaqami et al, was implemented and compared to deep learning (DL)-based models using convolutional neural networks to classify images generated from raw EEG signals. The models were trained and tested on pediatric EEGs acquired at the University Hospital in Essen. The DL model showed higher observed sensitivity (78.3%) and F 1 -score (80%) compared to the gradient boosting model (sensitivity: 65.2%; F 1 -score: 73.8%), indicating improved detection of abnormal EEGs. However, the gradient boosting approach achieved higher specificity (93% vs 89.6%), suggesting a stronger ability to recognize normal EEGs. Overall, both methods yielded promising results, with classification accuracies reaching up to 85.3%. Both approaches show potential for automated EEG interpretation. Future improvements, including larger and more diverse datasets, refined DL architectures, and integration of explainable AI techniques, could further enhance performance.

items.title: Single-nucleus transcriptomics reveals cardiomyocyte injury and fibro-inflammatory remodeling in early PKP2-deficient ARVC.
items.abstract: Arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy (ARVC) is an inherited cardiomyopathy caused primarily by mutations in desmosomal genes, among which pathogenic PKP2 variants being the most common genetic cause. Previous studies on ARVC have mainly focus on its middle and late pathological stages, whereas the early cellular and molecular events triggered by PKP2 loss remain poorly defined. We generated a cardiomyocyte-specific Pkp2 knockout mouse line and performed single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq) to delineate the early cellular landscape of ARVC. PKP2 loss triggered pathological remodeling of cardiomyocytes and induced a large-scale phenotypic shift in cardiac fibroblasts from a homeostatic state to an activated, matrix-producing population. Concomitantly, proangiogenic endothelial subsets expanded and Ccr2 + /Spp1 + proinflammatory macrophages accumulated, reshaping the cardiac microenvironment. Cell-cell communication network analysis demonstrated enhanced intercellular crosstalk at the early stage of ARVC, with aberrant activation of profibrotic and inflammatory signaling pathways. By integrating transcriptomic analysis, immunofluorescence staining and ligand-receptor interaction analysis, we identified CCN2 may serve as a potential mediator in early-stage PKP2-related ARVC. Our study proposes a multicellular relay model of early ARVC pathogenesis and identifies CCN2 as a putative intercellular communication factor in PKP2-deficient hearts. These findings highlight intercellular communication networks as critical mediators of disease progression and potential therapeutic targets.
items.journal: Journal of molecular and cellular cardiology

items.title: Consolidation With Hyper-CVAD or VP Plus Dasatinib in Philadelphia Chromosome-Positive Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
items.abstract: For Ph+ acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) patients achieving complete molecular response (CMR) pre-transplantation is critical, particularly for those ineligible for bispecific antibodies or CAR-T therapy. To compare the efficacy of 2-4 cycles of VP versus Hyper-CVAD with dasatinib as consolidation therapy in Ph+ ALL. This single-center, randomized controlled trial (NCT05026229) enrolled patients aged ≥ 18 years with de novo Ph+ ALL. After 1 cycle of VP (vincristine plus prednisone) plus dasatinib induction, patients were randomized to VP (Arm A) or Hyper-CVAD Part B (high-dose methotrexate and high-dose cytarabine, Arm B) consolidation. Primary endpoint was CMR after cycle 4. Secondary endpoints included CMR rate after cycle 2, CIR, PFS, OS and safety. 31 patients were enrolled before early termination due to excess relapse in the Arm A. For Arm A and Arm B, after cycle 2, CMR rates were 5.6% and 53.8%, and after cycle 4, CMR rates were 5.6% and 69.2%, respectively. With a median follow-up of 40 months, 3-year OS and PFS of Arm A and Arm B were 68.2% versus 57.1% (P = .16), and 31.8% versus 54.8%, respectively (P = .022). In Ph+ ALL patients ineligible for cellular immunotherapy, Hyper-CVAD demonstrated superior CMR rates, lower relapse risk, and significantly improved PFS compared with VP, despite no OS difference. The VP arm was terminated early due to high relapse rates, suggesting VP is not recommended as a preferred strategy in this population.

items.title: Immunotherapy mediated pituitary toxicity: current knowledge and priorities for care.
items.abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitor related pituitary toxicity (pituitary irAE) remains a relatively common complication of treatment which has transformed prognosis in several solid organ malignancies. While it may present with clear and clinically significant adrenal insufficiency, diagnostic uncertainty can remain due its potentially subtle clinical phenotype and symptom overlap with other treatment related effects. Currently pituitary irAE lacks a validated biomarker or single unifying pathophysiological model. This review aims to outline what is known regarding pathogenesis, presentation, biomarkers and long-term outcomes of pituitary irAE to inform future directions and priorities for care and research. Emerging data suggest multiple plausible immune pathways, including activation of pre-existing autoimmunity, direct checkpoint-mediated pituitary toxicity, paraneoplastic immune responses and cytokine-driven injury, but these mechanisms likely vary between patients. This review also explores current and future clinical priorities for hormone replacement, patient education and ongoing endocrine follow-up. As survival improves for patients receiving immune checkpoint inhibitors, improved phenotyping, biomarker development and long-term outcomes research will be essential to refine diagnosis, prognostication and survivorship care.

items.title: Emerging HER2-targeted treatment approaches for gastroesophageal cancer in the era of chemo-immunotherapy.
items.abstract: Human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2) is a key therapeutic target in gastroesophageal adenocarcinoma (GEA) and its targeting agents form the backbone of treatment for HER2-positive disease. Therapeutic options have expanded from the HER2-targeting antibody trastuzumab to antibody-drug conjugates (ADC). HER2-directed small-molecule inhibitors and bispecific HER2-directed compounds are under evaluation in treatment-naive and previously treated patients across different stages of disease. Beyond combinations with chemotherapy, combinations with immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICI) are of particular interest due to potential synergistic mechanisms, including antigen release, immune-cell recruitment, and antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity resulting in enhanced antitumor immunity. The current standard of care for HER2- and PD-L1-positive metastatic GEA (mGEA) combines chemotherapy with the HER2-targeting antibody trastuzumab and the PD-1-targeting ICI pembrolizumab. In the second-line setting, the ADC trastuzumab deruxtecan has further improved outcomes for these patients. Despite these advances and the emergence of new therapeutic options, several challenges remain, including optimal patient and drug selection, treatment sequencing, and the management of acquired resistance. Advances in liquid biopsy approaches, including the analysis of circulating tumor DNA, may facilitate longitudinal disease monitoring and guide personalized treatment strategies. This review summarizes the current and evolving role of HER2-targeted therapies in GEA, examines the growing integration of immunotherapy, and discusses future directions.

items.title: Model-informed precision dosing of busulfan in Adults: Real world implications for Dosing and Transplant outcomes.
items.abstract: Busulfan has been a cornerstone of conditioning regimens for hematopoietic cell transplantation (HCT) for decades. Systemic busulfan exposure has been associated with clinical outcomes. Both underexposure and overexposure carry risks of relapse and graft failure on one hand, and toxicity or non-relapse mortality on the other. Model-informed precision dosing (MIPD), based on early pharmacokinetic measurements, has been introduced to optimize individual exposure and improve outcomes. This study aims to evaluate the impact of MIPD on transplantation outcomes in adults treated at a large medical center. This retrospective cohort study included adult patients who underwent allogeneic HCT for malignant diseases between 1/1/2010 and 31/12/2022. Patients were divided into two groups based on the intravenous busulfan dosing strategy, a body weight-based dosing group (1/1/2010 to 31/12/2017) and a MIPD group (31/12/2017 to 31/12/2022). Busulfan plasma concentrations were measured after the first dose and analyzed using the NextDose platform to guide individualized dosing. The cumulative target AUC over 4 days was 79 mgh/L. Transplantation and disease related variables, toxicity (CTCAE grade 3-4 by day 100), and graft-versus-host disease (GVHD) were recorded. Survival outcomes included overall survival (OS), event-free survival (EFS), GVHD-free relapse-free survival (GRFS), relapse-free survival (RFS), and non-relapse mortality (NRM). Multivariable logistic regression, Cox proportional hazards models, and competing risk analyses using Fine-Gray models were applied. Among 107 patients, 62 received weight-based busulfan and 45 received MIPD. Baseline characteristics were largely comparable, although the MIPD group had a different ethnic distribution (p=0.007) and a lower Karnofsky score (p=0.024). Survival outcomes favored the MIPD group with OS (p=0.004), EFS (p=0.0053) and GRFS (p=0.0047). Higher conditioning intensity (dual alkylating agents) was associated with lower relapse in both groups (p=0.040, 0.011) and with improved OS only in the weight-based dosing group (p<0.001). Mucositis was more frequent with MIPD (p<0.001), and GVHD rates were similar between groups. In multivariable Cox regression analysis, MIPD (HR 0.40; p=0.009) and conditioning intensity (HR 0.37; p=0.003) were independently associated with improved OS. Competing risk analysis showed significantly lower non-relapse mortality in the MIPD group (p=0.009), but no significant difference in relapse probability (p=0.44). Our study compared weight-based dosing and MIPD of busulfan in adults undergoing allogeneic HCT. Transplantation outcomes were improved due to reduced mortality in the busulfan MIPD cohort. These finding highlight the potential of individualized dosing strategies to improve the therapeutic balance in transplantation.

items.title: When cord blood grafts may be the preferred donor choice: a position statement from the ASTCT Cord Blood Special Interest Group.
items.abstract: The introduction and wide adoption of post-transplant cyclophosphamide-based graft-versus host disease (GVHD) prophylaxis has changed the landscape of allograft donor selection such that allograft candidates now commonly have multiple potential graft sources, and there can be uncertainty over which graft source to prioritize. This position statement, written by the American Society for Transplantation and Cellular Therapy Cord Blood (CB) Special Interest Group and leading CB transplant physicians in the United States and abroad, discusses the state-of-the-art in CB transplantation (CBT). We highlight recent outcome data from multiple domestic and international centers with CBT expertise, across both adult and pediatric settings. Applying these data, we outline 4 clinical scenarios where CB may be the graft of choice: patients who lack a suitable, young, readily available donor, those in need of urgent transplantation, patients with difficult-to-cure acute leukemia or myelodysplastic syndrome, and patients with non-malignant diseases. We also present potential mechanisms underlying the unique graft-versus-leukemia effects mediating reduced relapse following CBT, along with the advantages of reduced chronic GVHD. This position statement emphasizes the critical, ongoing role of CBT in the transplant field, and will help guide transplant physicians to consider CBT as a preferred donor (or, as needed, referral to a center with CBT expertise) for patients in these scenarios.
authors: American Society for Transplantation and Cellular Therapy Cord Blood Special Interest Group

items.title: Analysis of the clinical features of Fitz-Hugh-Curtis syndrome: A retrospective case series study.
items.abstract: ObjectiveFitz-Hugh-Curtis syndrome is a form of perihepatic inflammation, frequently associated with pelvic inflammatory disease, primarily affecting the liver capsule without significant involvement of the hepatic parenchyma. This case series study aimed to investigate the clinical characteristics, treatment methods, and outcomes of Fitz-Hugh-Curtis syndrome to provide diagnostic and therapeutic insights for clinicians.MethodsThis single-center study retrospectively reviewed the clinical data of seven patients diagnosed with Fitz-Hugh-Curtis syndrome at the Southern University of Science and Technology Hospital between January 2021 and June 2024. The case series study summarized the patients' symptoms, signs, laboratory results, imaging findings, preliminary diagnoses, treatments, and outcomes.ResultsAmong the seven patients, five were women of reproductive age, and two were men. Six patients presented with acute abdominal pain, while one male patient remained asymptomatic with postoperative jejunal stromal tumor. Abdominal enhanced computed tomography was used to confirm the diagnosis of Fitz-Hugh-Curtis syndrome in all patients. Vaginal swabs from female patients identified Chlamydia trachomatis in two cases and Ureaplasma urealyticum in two other cases treatment based on individualized plans resulted in complete recovery in all patients.ConclusionsFitz-Hugh-Curtis syndrome should be considered in women of childbearing age presenting with right upper abdominal pain combined with right lower abdominal pain. Abdominal enhanced computed tomography plays a crucial role in the early initial diagnosis of Fitz-Hugh-Curtis syndrome.
items.journal: The Journal of international medical research

items.title: Metabolic Dysfunction as a Rising Barrier to HBV Elimination.
items.abstract: About one-third of patients with chronic hepatitis B (CHB) have hepatic steatosis, and cardiometabolic risk factors are increasingly prevalent. This review examines what metabolic dysfunction does to the measurements on which the elimination cascade depends, from prevention through diagnosis, treatment eligibility, on-treatment risk control, and functional cure to postcure surveillance. Metabolic dysfunction lowers the response to adult vaccination, enters three of the four routes to treatment eligibility in the World Health Organization criteria, contributes to the hepatocellular carcinoma risk that persists during antiviral therapy, and is absent from most risk scores and surveillance rules used before and after hepatitis B surface antigen loss. Its two components diverge: hepatic steatosis and cardiometabolic burden appear to additively increase the probability of hepatitis B surface antigen loss, but act in opposite directions on cirrhosis, hepatocellular carcinoma, and mortality. Assessing and correcting metabolic dysfunction as part of CHB care, and including patients with CHB in trials of metabolic therapy, would allow success to be defined by liver outcomes rather than by the virus alone.

items.title: Role of AngioVac in the Management of Severe MRSA Tricuspid Endocarditis With Multisystem Complications.
items.abstract: Right-sided infective endocarditis (IE) caused by methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) in people who inject drugs often causes septic pulmonary emboli and critical illness, and many of these patients are too unstable for cardiac surgery when they present. We report a 38-year-old woman with active intravenous drug use, untreated hepatitis C, and a seizure disorder who presented with MRSA bacteremia, a large tricuspid valve vegetation, and cavitary septic pulmonary emboli complicated by respiratory failure, shock, and empyema. Despite 33 days of antibiotics, she remained febrile with progressive pulmonary complications, and cardiothoracic surgery judged her too high risk for valve replacement. She underwent percutaneous vegetation debulking with the AngioVac system through femoral venous access, with removal of approximately 80% of the vegetation and no procedural complications. Her subsequent course included massive hemoptysis with cardiac arrest, bronchial artery embolization, video-assisted thoracoscopic decortication, tracheostomy, and gastrostomy, after which she stabilized and was discharged to a long-term acute care hospital. Approximately 3 months later, she underwent tricuspid valve replacement and survived the operation. This case shows how percutaneous aspiration can serve as a bridge to definitive valve surgery in critically ill patients with right-sided IE who are not initial surgical candidates, and it highlights the multidisciplinary care these patients need.
items.journal: Journal of investigative medicine high impact case reports

items.title: Seronegative hepatitis E associated with fatal acute-on-chronic liver failure in an anti-CD20-treated patient.
Direct Remnant Lipoprotein Profiling Reveals Subfraction-Level Associations with Biopsy-Proven MASH in Severe Obesity.
items.abstract: Directly measured remnant cholesterol (RC) has been linked to hepatic histological activity, but subfraction associations with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) in severe obesity remain unclear. We examined these associations, compared direct markers with estimated RC, and assessed added information beyond clinical variables. This cross-sectional study included 380 adults with severe obesity undergoing bariatric surgery; 110 had MASH. Vertical Auto Profile (VAP) quantified remnant subfractions. Multivariable logistic regression assessed associations. Incremental information was assessed by the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), continuous net reclassification improvement (NRI), and integrated discrimination improvement (IDI). An exploratory four-variable model was bootstrap-validated. Measured RC was independently associated with MASH (fully adjusted odds ratio [OR] per standard deviation, 1.32; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.05-1.67), whereas estimated RC was not. Among direct subfractions, very-low-density lipoprotein 3 cholesterol (VLDL3-C) showed the most consistent association (OR, 1.36; 95% CI, 1.08-1.70; P < 0.01), whereas intermediate-density lipoprotein cholesterol was significant only after fuller adjustment. All three direct markers produced similarly modest gains in discrimination, NRI, and IDI, with no clear differences in head-to-head comparisons. VLDL3-C was therefore selected for an exploratory four-variable model based on its consistent association and favorable model fit, achieving an optimism-corrected AUC of 0.724. At the lower cutoff, 34.5% of participants were classified as low risk, with 90.0% sensitivity and a negative predictive value of 91.6%. VAP profiling links remnant-related cholesterol to MASH at the subfraction level. VLDL3-C warrants further evaluation for risk assessment.

items.title: FXR-FGF15/19 STAT5 Signaling Coordinates Hepatocyte Protection and Immune Resolution in LCA-Induced Cholestatic Liver Injury.
items.abstract: Background: Cholangiopathies, such as primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC) involve bile acid toxicity, epithelial injury, and innate immune activation. While FXR regulates bile acid homeostasis, it remains unknown whether different FXR agonists elicit distinct protective responses. To determine whether early FXR activation can prevent the development of lithocholic acid (LCA)-induced cholestatic injury, we administered FXR agonists during LCA exposure and evaluated their effects on hepatocyte, immune, and endocrine responses. Methods: Adult male C57BL/6 mice were fed a 1%; LCA diet for 2 days and treated by intravenous infusion with FXR agonists GW4064 (30 mg/kg/day) or obeticholic acid (OCA; 20 mg/kg/day) for 4 days, initiated 2 days before LCA exposure. Liver injury was assessed by serum biochemistry, histology, immunostaining, intrahepatic mononuclear cell profiling, ChIP assay, and bulk liver RNA sequencing. Huh7 and T84 cells were used for co-culture. Results: LCA induced marked cholestatic injury with elevated liver enzymes, bile duct injury, macrophage and neutrophil infiltration, and activation of inflammatory, oxidative stress, apoptotic, and MYC-dependent transcriptional programs. FXR agonists prevented biochemical and histologic injury, restored hepatocyte bile acid transport and feedback regulation, reduced oxidative stress and apoptosis, and attenuated coordinated macrophage-neutrophil activation. Transcriptomic analyses revealed agonist-dependent effects, with GW4064 and OCA suppressing LCA-induced injury pathways. FXR activation induced ileal FXR targets and Fgf15 , reduced intestinal macrophage infiltration, and activated hepatic STAT5 signaling. Direct FGF19 treatment of Huh7 cells recapitulated hepatocyte protective effects and STAT5 activation. Conclusions: FXR agonist treatment mitigates LCA-induced cholestatic liver injury by restoring hepatocyte bile acid homeostasis, suppressing innate immune inflammation, and engaging an ileal FXR-FGF15/19-hepatic STAT5 survival axis, with distinct agonist-dependent transcriptional outcomes.
items.journal: American journal of physiology. Gastrointestinal and liver physiology

items.title: A window-of-opportunity trial testing single-dose neoadjuvant hepatic arterial floxuridine and oxaliplatin for patients with localized pancreatic cancer: analysis of safety, feasibility, and interim oncologic outcomes.
items.abstract: Recurrence is common following curative-intent therapy for localized pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC), with the liver representing the most frequent site of relapse. Neoadjuvant hepatic artery (HA) chemotherapy improved outcomes in localized colorectal cancer. We evaluated the safety and feasibility of this approach in localized PDAC. This prospective, non-randomized trial treated 20 patients with localized PDAC with a single dose of neoadjuvant HA floxuridine (325 mg/m 2 ) and oxaliplatin (37.5 mg/m 2 ) one week before surgical resection. Primary endpoints were 30-day safety and feasibility. Secondary endpoints include three-year disease-free (DFS), liver metastasis-free (LMFS), and overall survival (OS). HA chemotherapy was successfully delivered in 20 of 21 patients (95.2%). While 14 patients (70%) experienced at least one adverse event within the safety period, only two were possibly related to treatment, including grade 1 and grade 2 transaminitis events that resolved without intervention. No serious adverse events were attributed to treatment. At a median follow up of 13.8 months, 16 patients remain alive (median OS not reached). Seven developed recurrence (median DFS 20.5 months), including four with liver metastases (median LMFS 20.5 months). Single-dose neoadjuvant HA chemotherapy is safe and feasible in localized PDAC. Long-term follow-up is ongoing.
items.journal: HPB : the official journal of the International Hepato Pancreato Biliary Association

items.title: Translocation of the environmental bacterium Aquitalea magnusonii promotes systemic inflammation and liver fibrosis in chronic liver disease.
items.abstract: Impaired mucosal barrier integrity facilitates translocation of the gut microbiome into the circulation and the liver, thereby exacerbating the severity of chronic liver diseases (CLD). This study aimed to investigate the pathogenic role of non-commensal environmental bacteria, specifically Aquitalea magnusonii in CLD progression by assessing its ability to cross the intestinal barrier and induce systemic inflammation and liver fibrosis. Using an integrated translational framework, patient blood analyses were combined with multi-omics profiling, human intestinal epithelial models, peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMC), hepatic stellate cells (HSC), monocytes, and alcoholic (ALD) and metabolic dysfunction-associated (MASLD) models to evaluate the translocation, virulence, inflammatory and fibrotic potential of A. magnusonii in CLD. Non-commensal environmental bacteria, including Aquitalea spp. were detected in multiple organs in both ALD and MASLD models. Detection of Aquitalea DNA in patient samples and other non-commensal environmental bacteria in tap water suggested potential aquatic reservoirs. A. magnusonii produced 12 acute-on-chronic liver failure (ACLF) associated metabolites and its outer membrane vesicles (OMV) were enriched in virulence-related proteins, supporting roles in adhesion, invasion, and immune activation. In addition, gavage with A. magnusonii led to a substantial dysbiotic shift in the gut microbiome. Mechanistically, the cell-free supernatant of A. magnusonii culture activated TLR2- and TLR4-dependent pro-inflammatory signaling pathways. Exposure to A. magnusonii or its pathogen-associated molecular patterns (PAMPs) significantly increased inflammation and fibrosis in vitro and in vivo. Non-commensal environmental bacteria, in the example of A. magnusonii, can translocate across the intestinal barrier and promote liver inflammation and fibrogenesis via metabolite production, virulence-associated OMV, and innate immune activation. This study highlights an underrecognized role of non-commensal environmental bacteria in chronic liver disease. Beyond gut commensals, detection of non-commensal environmental microbes such as Aquitalea was associated with markers of more advanced liver disease, while experimental studies of A. magnusonii support biological plausibility for a potential contributory role. These findings highlight the importance of considering environmental reservoirs and non-commensal pathogens in microbial contributions to CLD pathogenesis.

items.title: Pre-Liver Transplant Immunotherapy and Post-Transplant Outcomes in HCC: Global LIFT-HCC-1 Study.
items.abstract: Use of immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) before liver transplantation (LT) for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains controversial with limited data on post-LT overall and recurrence-free survival (OS and RFS). We aimed to investigate factors associated with long-term post-LT outcomes in ICI-treated LT patients. This global study analyzed ICI-treated HCC patients who underwent LT between 2015-2025. Determinants of allograft rejection, HCC recurrence, and OS were assessed using Cox proportional hazards and Fine-Gray competing-risk models with follow-up starting at LT, with hazard ratios (HRs) or subdistribution hazard ratios (SHRs). Of 408 patients, 23% met Milan criteria at ICI initiation, rising to 43% at LT. During a median follow-up of 21.2 (95%CI,18.9-25.4) months after LT, rejection, recurrence, and death occurred in 19%, 26%, and 21%, respectively. Non-HBV etiologies (HCV: aSHR=3.86; non-viral: aSHR=2.55) and irAEs (aSHR=1.87, 95%CI=1.11-3.14) were associated with higher rejection risk, whereas older age (aSHR per 10 years=0.74, 95%CI=0.58-0.94) and washout >90 days (aSHR=0.49, 95%CI=0.26-0.93) reduced this risk. AFP≥20 (aSHR=2.14, 95%CI=1.27-3.61) and being outside Milan at LT (aSHR=2.17, 95%CI=1.12-4.17) were associated with recurrence. Severe rejection (aHR=6.09, 95%CI=2.05-18.1) and HCC recurrence (aHR=15.9, 95%CI=7.08-35.9) were associated with shorter OS. No significant difference in outcomes was observed between patients with downstaged HCC and those always within Milan criteria, with comparable 3-year OS (80.8% vs 86.9%, p=0.92) and RFS (83.8% vs 86.5%, p=0.88). Tumor burden and AFP at LT were associated with HCC recurrence. Higher rejection risk was associated with non-HBV etiology, irAEs, younger age, and shorter ICI washout period. Larger prospective studies with control groups should validate these findings.
items.journal: Clinical gastroenterology and hepatology : the official clinical practice journal of the American Gastroenterological Association

items.title: Role of Ces1f/TGH-2 in adiposity and hepatic steatosis upon fasting.
items.abstract: Adaptive response to fasting plays an important role in whole-body energy metabolism under nutritional stress. Carboxylesterases comprise a family of serine esterases that hydrolyze xenobiotic compounds and endogenous lipids. Of particular interest in view of energy metabolism are human carboxylesterase 1/triacylglycerol hydrolase (CES1/TGH), and its mouse counterparts, Ces1d/TGH-1 and Ces1f/TGH-2. These esterases are unique in that they are highly expressed in the liver and adipose tissues and have substantial TGH activity. Notably, Ces1d and Ces1f are PPARα targets and regulated by fasting. While deficiency of Ces1d or pharmacological inhibition of Ces1d/Ces1f in mice has been shown to ameliorate features of metabolic syndrome, the physiological role of Ces1f has not been clarified in vivo. Here we show that Ces1f plays an important role in whole-body and hepatic fat metabolism upon fasting in a diet-dependent manner. On a normal diet, Ces1f-deficient (Ces1f -/- ) mice presented with increased adiposity and exacerbated hepatic steatosis. On a high-fat diet, Ces1f -/- mice presented with decreased adiposity and ameliorated hepatic steatosis. Mechanistically, the differential balance between decreased adipose TGH activity and, possibly, increased liver fatty acid oxidation (FAO) in Ces1f -/- at least partially explains the diet-context dependency. Decreased adiposity in Ces1f -/- mice under a high-fat diet was associated with improved glucose tolerance. Collectively, these findings revealed the unique role of Ces1f in whole-body response to fasting by modulating adipocyte lipolysis and, at least partially, hepatic FAO genes. Our study provides a molecular foundation for understanding CES1 inhibitors, which have potential therapeutic implications for metabolic diseases and liver cancer. (250 words).
